title: Final Dependency Vulnerability Resolution

advisories.cve: CVE-2026-59870? (npm advisory record names the package advisory as GHSA-pm4m-ph32-ghv5; exact CVE mapping is advisory-specific and not separately asserted here)

advisories.direct_or_transitive: transitive dependency of attempted downgrade path

remediation_attempted: Re-verified the current registry and install tree.
Confirmed the latest stable @nestjs/swagger remains 11.4.6 and still depends on js-yaml 5.2.1.
Checked whether a package override to js-yaml 5.2.3 can resolve the issue.
Attempted a downgrade path to @nestjs/swagger 11.4.5 to reach js-yaml 4.3.0, which remained vulnerable under a different advisory.
No safe supported fix was found within the current stable @nestjs/swagger release line.

production_reachability_assessment.enabled_in_production: Swagger is present in the backend application and may be enabled in non-production or controlled admin/dev environments, but the advisory is not a direct user request-path vulnerability in the app's business logic.
production_reachability_assessment.yaml_parsing_exposure: The vulnerability is associated with the transitive js-yaml dependency used by @nestjs/swagger, not with application-owned YAML parsing of customer requests.
production_reachability_assessment.runtime_exploitability: Residual risk is real at the dependency level, but the app's direct production request path is not the same as parsing arbitrary YAML content from user input.
production_reachability_assessment.classification: Upstream dependency blocker with limited application-level exploitability; unresolved in the currently supported stable package tree.
